name: Timeline
intent: Force sequence and expose what must happen before what.
when: planning, or when the human is secretly trying to do everything at once
prompt: Put things in order. What must be true before what?
readback: Find any two items with no ordering relation — that is the ambiguity to resolve.

claims.claim: Breaking a task into its ordered component steps before predicting when it will be done reduces optimistic bias in completion-time predictions.

grounding.helps: when a task has many parts and you are tempted to guess its end date whole: writing the steps out in order makes the work visible before you commit to a time, though no study tests ordering steps as this page does
grounding.backfires: when the steps turn into a story of how everything will go right, since plan-focused scenarios are what make time predictions too optimistic, and when the finish date is set without comparing it with how long similar work took before
